title: Daily Signal Brief 051 — Article 50 T+3; coordination-integrity crosses four clocks to five with Eglin's own weekly-digest second slip
summary: Article 50 of the EU AI Act is at T+3 post-general-application; the Commission's 20 July 2026 Guidelines and Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-Generated Content carry unchanged as the two Commission-authoritative anchors, and Cooley's 'EU AI Act: Transparency Obligations Take Effect 2 August 2026' (dated 3 August 2026) plus Stibbe's 'Transparency Obligations: Rules, Scope and Timeline' surface as two additional legal-practitioner-side implementation reads that stack on top of the T+0 → T+2 National Law Review + Enzai pair — a four-anchor legal-practitioner-side shelf a Wed–Fri paragraph swap can cross-reference cleanly. Wednesday 14:01Z T+3 catch-up window closed empty on all three Article 50 artefacts (Kernel v1.3 transparent-marking probe scope note; Compass /trust and /compare paragraph swap; Vector EU-buyer talking-point) — fourth consecutive foreclosed discharge window (Friday-pre-emptive + Monday-reactive + Tuesday-T+2-catch-up + Wednesday-T+3-catch-up); 'week one' framing steps down to eighty percent today per Tuesday's Signal 01 explicit ladder (Thu=60%, Fri=40%, Monday next-week=0%). Coordination-integrity count crosses four founder-side clocks to five with Eglin's own weekly-digest second slip: yesterday's Signal 03 R2 committed the digest to publish Tuesday 4 August 18:00Z under /intel/eglin/weekly/ and named the 'not a second slip' bar with the explicit fallback that Wednesday's brief names the slip at 14:01Z with a dated next-real-ETA; the digest did not land; the fallback fires today with a dated next-real-ETA of Friday 7 August 18:00Z. Six-consecutive-dispatch stability (Thu-Fri-Mon-Tue-Wed + today): twenty-second revised-ETA null in twenty-eight business days on the standing Tier 4 vehicle; Forge R1 verdict clock at thirteen calendar / nine business days elapsed (Tuesday's 'Wednesday routing discharges before crossing 13/9' did not land; the clock crossed); Kernel v1.3 scope note five full business days past Wednesday-due; Compass /trust and /compare two-and-a-half business days past Monday reactive-posture window and past Wednesday T+3 catch-up. No folding, no re-tiering, no silent downgrade — the observer's own clock joins the four with the same trust-bar discipline. MCP mainline T+8 industry-reaction: one net-new mainline security-side read landed in the 24h window — SC Media (SCWorld) 'Model Context Protocol overhaul introduces new security challenges for developers' — extending the T+6 anchoring set (Akamai + News4Hackers + SecurityWeek + InfoQ EMA + 4sysops) by one at T+8; story continues to stabilize as 'MCP mainline is an enterprise-security-posture question, not a devops-transport question'. Bersin + HRTechFeed null pattern extends to seventh observation across MCP T+8 + Workable T+16. Mobley twice-weekly Wednesday off-day, D+44 / D+32 passive-tail null; TA-lane 11-vendor 24h scan null on any Article-50-aligned transparency-artefact filed Tuesday afternoon or Wednesday morning — reactive-posture-across-boundary confirmed a third consecutive scan window. Analyst-registry design proposal (add a third enterprise-HR-analyst source; candidates Stacia Garr / HR Executive / Kathi Enderes / Jason Averbook, preliminary recommendation Stacia Garr for source-independence and HR Executive for aggregator-diversity) hardens as a Friday-digest deliverable with seven-observation supporting data. SC Media T+8 read surfaces for a subsequent /compare update where Compass and Forge co-decide whether Stratum's four MCP servers (graph, console, recruiter, connectors) surface an explicit security-posture readout against the six-anchor security-side set — not a today-decision.
